source.check: returned without a contest: the nominations gave contests only in Ardglass and Ballynahinch (Dromore Leader, 21 May 1949, p. 3); elected vice-chairman at the annual meeting of the new council, Saturday 11 June 1949 (Frontier Sentinel, 18 June 1949, p. 5: 'Mr. James Hurst, vice-chairman'; Dromore Leader, 18 June 1949, p. 3: 'Mr. James Hurst, J.P. ..., vice-chairman') (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Downpatrick rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. The News-Letter reports contests at Ballynahinch and Ardglass, where the Nationalists gained a seat from Labour. Ballynahinch Rural is recorded from reports of the new council's annual meeting of 11 June 1949, with its division from the 1930 return (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 3 May 1930 return (J. Hurst, J.P., Ballynahinch Rural), the last that names the member for the division; the council-meeting reports cited name the member as sitting at the new council's first meeting, and the Dromore Leader places him in that division. The three other members named at the meeting (John Jennings, Thomas Jennings, William Glover) were co-opted, not elected. Returned unopposed.
